evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We run a community health agent program in two districts of Zambia's Copperbelt. Outcome we're accountable to the funder for: fewer unintended pregnancies among women 18 to 35 in our catchment by end of 2027. Activities: 60 community health agents trained for two days on counseling; each agent gets a stock of condoms to sell at a small margin; agents do home visits in their zone roughly twice a month; a supervisor collects sales data monthly. Population: agents are mostly women 25 to 45 from the villages; the outcome is for women 18 to 35 and their partners. Evidence we have: 8 months of sales data (median agent sells 30 packs a month, a quarter sell under 5), and an evidence review we commissioned in 2024, which found that the studies of selling condoms through community agents are mostly from cities and none is from rural Zambia. Write our theory of change.
evals.expected_output: A theory of change in the output template whose chain runs from the agents' activities through named behaviors of agents and couples to fewer unintended pregnancies.
assertions: Carries the outcome over as the user stated it.
Every link has an assumption in if-then-because form and one of the four strength labels.
Evidence cells cite only the sales data or the 2024 review; no other study is cited.
No link that rests on the 2024 review is labeled above 'tested elsewhere'.
Lists behaviors for both agents and couples, each with a link number and marked confirmed or inferred.
Names the link from buying condoms to using them as a weak link with no evidence supplied.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Can you write a theory of change for our program?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the outcome, the activities as delivered, and the population, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks what outcome the program is accountable for.
Asks what the program does, by whom, to whom.
Asks who the activities reach or who the outcome is for.
Does not produce a causal chain table.
Does not invent a program or fill the template with placeholders.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: Our Ministry of Health partner in Malawi wants to scale our antenatal iron-folate adherence program nationally next year and needs a theory of change for the cabinet paper. Outcome: lower maternal anemia at delivery. Activities: clinics hand out a month's supply at each visit; community health workers do monthly village visits and remind women to take the tablet daily; we send a weekly SMS to women with phones. Population: pregnant women at 40 rural clinics; CHWs and clinic nurses deliver. Evidence: our own pill counts from four pilot clinics (under a third of women adherent); no evidence review done; the CHW reminder link is something we believe works but have not tested. Please draft it.
evals.expected_output: The skill drafts the chain with the reminder link labeled an assumption, and tells the user to bring in an evaluation specialist and a clinician before the chain goes into the cabinet paper.
assertions: Produces the causal chain table.
Labels the link from reminders to daily tablet-taking 'assumption'.
Evidence cells contain only the pill counts or 'none supplied'.
Tells the user to consult an evaluation specialist because the chain will justify a national scale-up.
Tells the user to consult a clinician because the chain runs through medication in pregnancy.
Says what to bring to the specialist.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Here is our theory of change for the M-Pesa vendor savings program in Nairobi (table pasted above). It runs through three behaviors: vendors deposit at the end of the day, vendors keep a written cash count, and vendors attend the weekly chama. Which one should we actually target first?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the chain already exists and the question is which behavior to target, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the theory of change already exists.
Names define-key-behavior.
Does not redraft the causal chain.
Does not pick one of the three behaviors itself.
